summary: Anthropic launched Claude Fable 5 (general-access) and Claude Mythos 5 (restricted, safeguards-lifted) as its most capable models to date, with new safety classifiers, a 30-day data retention policy for Mythos-class traffic, and pricing of $10/$50 per million input/output tokens.

mechanisms.reason: The lab states this is its most capable generally-available model, state-of-the-art on nearly all tested benchmarks.
mechanisms.quote: Fable 5’s capabilities exceed those of any model we’ve ever made generally available. It is state-of-the-art on nearly all tested benchmarks of AI capability

mechanisms.reason: The document states the model is more token-efficient than prior Claude models, implying lower compute per unit of output.
mechanisms.quote: Fable 5 is also more token-efficient than past Claude models

mechanisms.reason: Access to both models was suspended shortly after launch and then redeployed, directly affecting served inference volume.
mechanisms.quote: We are suspending access to Claude Fable 5 and Claude Mythos 5. We apologize for this disruption to our customers and are working to restore access as soon as possible.

mechanisms.reason: The model is described as maintaining focus and using persistent memory across millions of tokens, increasing context/cache demands.
mechanisms.quote: Fable 5 stays focused across millions of tokens in long-running tasks and improves its outputs using its own notes.

mechanisms.reason: The announcement frames the model as enabling developers to delegate increasingly ambitious, long-horizon work to autonomous agents.
mechanisms.quote: a future where developers can hand increasingly ambitious work to agents and trust the results across the software lifecycle

practices.reason: A frontier release with stated gains in coding, reasoning, and vision tasks changes what teams could deploy for production workloads.
practices.quote: showing exceptional performance in software engineering, knowledge work, vision, scientific research, and many other areas

practices.reason: Named third-party benchmarks (FrontierCode, CursorBench, Hebbia Finance Benchmark) give engineering teams concrete instruments to validate model quality against their own workloads.
practices.quote: Claude Fable 5 is the state of the art model on CursorBench.

practices.reason: The new mandatory 30-day data retention policy for Mythos-class traffic requires compliance and logging changes for any team integrating the API.
practices.quote: We will require 30-day retention for all traffic on Mythos-class models, on both first- and third-party surfaces.

practices.reason: The described persistent file-based memory pattern shows a stated performance gain but is demonstrated only in the lab's own game-playing test, not a general recipe.
practices.quote: giving it access to persistent file-based memory improved its performance three times more than for Opus 4.8

notable_reason: A frontier model launch with a novel tiered-safeguard architecture (general model falling back to a prior model on risky queries) and a brief post-launch outage is unusual and consequential enough to warrant direct attention.
